reachable: Yes, and verified on real data with the real harness plumbing rather than by reading. (1) Segmentation: prev = cat([zeros, tgt[:,:-1]]) masked by cmd_mask is exactly zero at, and only at, a trajectory's first flattened row — _segments' ids matched the true trajectory ids element-for-element on 9 different real batches (3 seeds x 3 curriculum steps), so the flatten is sequence-major and contiguous as claimed. (2) Detection: the relocation detector fires on 171/1886 rows (9.07%, claimed ~9%) and selects 64/64 cups_test rows, 101/193 cvar_test rows and 6 strays. Across 3 seeds x 3 steps x class caps 4/6/8/12/20 it selects 100% of cups_test rows every single time, with 2-15 strays — the cap-insensitivity claim holds. cups_test is the training-split analogue of the scored read, so the mechanism acts exactly where comp_ca is measured. (3) The equivalence relation is correct: against the true rendered observation strings it produced 48 false-merge pairs out of 396,298 (all of them strings differing only in trailing whitespace, which the encoder maps to the same vector) and ZERO missed pairs. The null-space claim reproduces exactly — a difference orthogonal to the sketch basis fools the sketch 200/200 and the conjunction 0/200 — and distinct vectors stay distinct down to 1e-5 relative squared distance, merging only at 1e-6 (the hypothesis says ~5e-5 and names 1e-6 as the failure point; both correct). (4) Gradient: the mechanism is NOT gated on an observation being present at the row it acts on — it is a target-side selector, so the 'command present, observation absent' hazard does not apply. On a real batch the new terms contribute 0.151 of a 0.666 total loss and raise the per-row gradient norm at relocation rows from 0.00005 to 0.00022 (~4.4x) versus the same loss with the new terms switched off. A real 40-step training run of the full genome on CPU completed with finite loss, passed the stream leakage probe, and cost 1.28 s/step.
solves_outside_model: No leak. The impl never parses a command string in Python — it touches commands only as frozen encoder embeddings, via cosine similarity, under torch.no_grad, to CHOOSE and WEIGHT negatives. Nothing is written into ctx, into the collated batch, or into any model input; loss() reads (pred, tgt, ctx) and returns a scalar, mutating none of them (the only in-place op is index_copy_ into a fresh zeros_like inside the ridge fit). The relocation selector and the address ring are built from the TARGETS, i.e. from the labels, which is ordinary supervised loss shaping — the same category as picking samples or reweighting rows, not the category of the prior retraction, where a resolved identity was stamped into the scored read token. The loss does not exist at scoring time, so no part of this machinery can reach the model at the scored position. I also checked the shortcut direction: the anti-name-partner pressure the ring creates is a function of board geometry, which is identical in the native and role-swapped arms, so it cancels in comp_ca and cannot inflate the score without genuine routing.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says it does, and unusually for a jailed inventor with no torch, its factual claims about the data and the mechanism survive execution against the real training root. I reproduced the whole training-side path with the real embedding cache (data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, 2560 sequences, standardized, split_train_dev, the genome's own batcher at bs=64) and measured: the trajectory segmentation is exact; the relocation detector fires on 9.07% of rows and captures 100% of cups_test reads with a handful of strays, stable across seeds, curriculum steps and class caps 4..20; the exact-duplicate test agrees with rendered-string equality with zero misses; the address ring's top negative is a same-board cups_expose in 60/64 cases, is never an mv step, and equals the lexically nearest command in 54/64 — i.e. it really does concentrate on the name-partner decoy the hypothesis names; and the new terms carry 23% of the loss and ~4.4x the per-row gradient at exactly those rows. The two headline mechanisms (a within-trajectory listwise contrast and a margin hinge, both in the eval's own unweighted mean-squared-distance geometry, both restricted to relocation rows) are implemented as described and match the eval's decision rule (realenv._rank_stats and cups_probe both pick argmin of ((cand - pred)**2).mean(-1)). Divergences are all quantitative colour rather than mechanism: the row boost is 3.07x, not the claimed ~6x, and does not 'undo' the class-size discount; the batch-wide head was re-implemented rather than inherited verbatim (though it reproduces the parent to 4e-6 on real data, with zero disagreeing equivalence pairs); the address ring is near one-hot rather than 'soft'; and the anti-collapse/timing absolutes quoted as measured reproduce on a synthetic gaussian batch but not on a real one. WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: whether any of this moves comp_ca. That needs the full 4000-step training and the scoring instrument on GPU, and at 1.28 s/step on CPU a single seed is ~85 minutes before scoring. I also could not check behaviour on the held-out-by-image val windows, the GPU-lane share of the added loss cost, or the interaction with the r23 arch's address/transport heads that §3 claims the new terms supervise — I verified the terms exist and get gradient, not that they reach those specific gates.

divergences.claim: "the row boost buys the compositional rows roughly 6x the gradient share they get today (3x boost against a 1/2 class-size discount)" and "undoing the 1/class_size down-weighting that currently taxes exactly these rows" (hypothesis §2, §4)
divergences.what_the_code_does: row_w = row_w * (1.0 + _RELOC_BOOST * reloc) with _RELOC_BOOST = 3.0, i.e. a 4x multiplier applied ON TOP of the 1/class_size discount, which is not undone. Measured on a real batch (n=1886, 171 relocation rows): the relocation rows' share of total row mass goes 0.1015 -> 0.3111, a 3.07x increase; per-row weight relative to the batch mean goes 1.119 -> 3.431. So the reallocation is ~3x, not ~6x, and these rows were not actually below-mean before the boost (the energy gate already lifts them).
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/checks.py CHECK2: 'reloc share of row mass: unboosted 0.1015 boosted 0.3111 ratio 3.07x; per-row relative weight vs mean: unboosted 1.119 boosted 3.431'

divergences.claim: §3: "Kept from the parent: ... the exact-target quotient with inverse-class mass" — i.e. the batch-wide head is the parent's, so any difference is attributable to the two new terms.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The quotient was reimplemented, not kept. The parent (r3_fwl_orthogonalized_ring_contrast) decides equivalence in the PRECISION-WEIGHTED space at _EQ_FRAC=1e-3 of the weighted mean, and scales the ring's duplicate suppression by that weighted mean. The child decides equivalence in RAW space with the 8-column DCT sketch at 1e-6 conjoined with a 2e-2 full-space check, and switches dup_scale from mean_raw to mean_plain. On real data this is a numerical no-op: 0 disagreeing pairs out of 1886^2, identical class sizes for all 1886 rows, and the child's loss with the new terms disabled reproduces the parent's to 4e-6 (0.514942 vs 0.514939). So the head is functionally kept, but the source is not the parent's and the attribution claim rests on a coincidence of thresholds rather than on identity of code.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/headdiff.py: 'parent vs child equivalence disagreement pairs: 0'; 'rows with different class size: 0 / 1886'; 'child(new terms off) 0.514942 parent 0.514939'; diff of the two impl files.

divergences.claim: §5: "the ring is soft precisely so the remaining mass is not wasted"
divergences.what_the_code_does: With _ADDR_TAU = 0.05 the address ring is close to one-hot where a lexical partner exists. Over the 64 cups_test relocation rows in a real batch the mean mass on the top candidate is 0.905 (max 1.000, min 0.271); mean entropy 0.24 nats. It is soft only in the ambiguous windows. This does not hurt the mechanism — the concentration lands on the intended decoy — but the described softness is not what the constant produces.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/ring.py: 'top mass mean 0.9047 min 0.2710 max 1.0; entropy mean 0.2423'. Example row: read cmd 'cat /tmp/w/cups/g14/f776.dat.4' -> q=0.995 on 'cat /tmp/w/cups/g14/f776.dat' (the name-partner).

divergences.claim: §6 measured numbers: anti-collapse 5.01 (zero) / 5.04 (mean) / 0.093 (near-perfect) on a 1920-row batch; loss fwd+bwd 0.105 s against the parent's 0.067 s at n=1920 on CPU.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Reproduces on a synthetic 1920-row gaussian batch with injected trajectory structure: 5.65 / 5.64 / 0.28, and timing child 0.105 s vs parent 0.078 s — the child's own timing matches to three digits, the parent baseline is understated by ~15%. On a REAL standardized batch (n=1886) the anti-collapse figures are 12.16 / 12.15 / 0.64 and the timing is 0.075 s vs 0.060 s. The qualitative claims (a constant prediction is an order of magnitude worse; the added cost is ~25-35% of a loss that is itself a small share of a training step) hold; the absolutes are batch-dependent and quoted from a synthetic setting without saying so.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/checks.py CHECK3/CHECK5 (real batch) and the synthetic rerun: 'zero 5.645 mean 5.643 near-perfect 0.277; timing child 0.105 parent 0.078'.
